stories.title: Scott Avenue housing proposal: public comments close today
stories.summary: The Town is seeking feedback on a potential multiunit residential development on vacant land between Mill Road and Carmelite Road. The published design is illustrative; no final project approval is established.
stories.why: This is a real chance to shape how existing serviced land becomes homes, while weighing neighbourhood character, access and long-term infrastructure costs.

stories.title: Red Maple Festival brings a full week of events to town
stories.summary: From October 29 through November 5, the Town’s festival brings together recreation, family activities, local arts, 50+ clubs, movies and a community bonfire across multiple venues.
stories.why: It is a practical example of GFW’s strength as a gathering place. Attendance and visitor spending are still unknown, but the programming spans generations and neighbourhoods.

stories.title: First Central NL highway-twinning construction tender is out
stories.summary: The Province issued a tender for 6.2 kilometres of subgrade work between the current divided highway near GFW and the Bishop’s Falls railway overpass. No contractor award has been established.
stories.why: Separately tendered contracts may offer regional contractors a more accessible route into major infrastructure work. The actual local capture will depend on bids, awards and subcontracting.

stories.title: Circular Road Phase II work continues
stories.summary: Watermain, storm sewer and road improvements between High Street and East Street may bring temporary service changes, detours and delays while work continues to approximately October 30.
stories.why: Keeping established streets and underground infrastructure reliable is as important to everyday livability as adding new subdivisions.

stories.title: Lincoln Road residential land proposal heads toward public hearing
stories.summary: Council has adopted proposed amendments to redesignate recreation open space off Lincoln Road for low- and medium-density residential use. Written representations are due November 16 ahead of a November 18 public hearing.
stories.why: The town needs housing, but also connected public spaces. The important test is whether residential development can preserve or improve active-transportation links.
